# Changelog

doc: CHANGELOG.md
section: Changelog > 1.4.0 (2025-03-14)
## 1.4.0 (2025-03-14)
- Retries cut from 5 to 3, with the delay starting at 0.5 s and doubling each time ([ADR 0001](docs/decisions/0001-retry-policy.md)).
- Events that fail all 3 retries now land in `dead_letters` and can be replayed through the admin API.

doc: CHANGELOG.md
section: Changelog > 1.3.0 (2025-01-22)
## 1.3.0 (2025-01-22)
- Moved the event queue from Postgres polling to Redis Streams ([ADR 0002](docs/decisions/0002-queue-choice.md)).

doc: README.md
section: PayMint
# PayMint

PayMint relays payment events from our payment gateway to merchant servers as webhooks. Every event goes onto a queue (Redis Streams), and if a merchant's server doesn't answer, PayMint retries a fixed number of times.

doc: README.md
section: PayMint > Running locally
## Running locally

You'll need Node.js 20 and Docker.

```bash
cp .env.example .env
docker compose up -d redis postgres
npm install
npm run dev
```

The server listens on `http://localhost:8080`. Health check: `GET /healthz`.

doc: README.md
section: PayMint > Tests
## Tests

```bash
npm test            # unit tests (vitest)
npm run test:e2e    # spins up a fake merchant server and runs the whole webhook flow
```

CI runs both on every PR. The e2e suite needs Redis, so run `docker compose up -d redis` first.

doc: docs/configuration.md
section: Configuration
# Configuration

Every setting can be overridden with an environment variable. Anything you don't set falls back to the default in `src/config.ts`.

doc: docs/configuration.md
section: Configuration > Server and storage
## Server and storage

| Variable | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PORT` | 8080 | API server port |
| `DATABASE_URL` | (none, required) | Postgres for merchant records and delivery history |
| `REDIS_URL` | `redis://localhost:6379` | Event queue (Redis Streams) |

doc: docs/configuration.md
section: Configuration > Retries and timeouts
## Retries and timeouts

| Variable | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PAYMINT_RETRY_MAX` | 3 | Max number of retries when a merchant's server fails. The first attempt doesn't count |
| `PAYMINT_RETRY_BASE_MS` | 500 | Starting retry delay. Doubles each time: 0.5 s, 1 s, 2 s |
| `PAYMINT_WEBHOOK_TIMEOUT_MS` | 3000 | How long to wait for the merchant's server to respond (3 s). Past that, it counts as a failure and is retried |

Why the retry count is 3: see [ADR 0001](decisions/0001-retry-policy.md).

doc: docs/configuration.md
section: Configuration > Signing and per-merchant settings
## Signing and per-merchant settings

| Variable | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PAYMINT_SIGNING_SECRET` | (dev only) | Fallback signing secret. In production each merchant's secret comes from the DB |

Each merchant's webhook URL and signing secret live in the `merchants` table. Change them with the admin API: `PATCH /admin/merchants/:id`.

doc: docs/decisions/0001-retry-policy.md
section: 0001. Retry policy: at most 3 retries, doubling from 0.5 s
# 0001. Retry policy: at most 3 retries, doubling from 0.5 s

- Status: accepted (2025-03-12)
- Decided by: Payments Platform team

doc: docs/decisions/0001-retry-policy.md
section: 0001. Retry policy: at most 3 retries, doubling from 0.5 s > Context
## Context

Merchant servers often go down for a moment and come right back. Before we had retries, merchants who missed a payment-complete webhook were contacting us about it several times a week.

doc: docs/decisions/0001-retry-policy.md
section: 0001. Retry policy: at most 3 retries, doubling from 0.5 s > Decision
## Decision

- On failure, retry at most 3 times (`PAYMINT_RETRY_MAX=3`).
- The delay starts at 0.5 s and doubles (0.5 s, 1 s, 2 s), with ±20% jitter so lots of events don't retry at the same instant.
- After 3 failed retries the event goes to `dead_letters`, and a person replays it.

doc: docs/decisions/0001-retry-policy.md
section: 0001. Retry policy: at most 3 retries, doubling from 0.5 s > Alternatives considered
## Alternatives considered

- 5 retries: a single failing merchant backed up the whole queue (the February 2025 incident). That's why we cut it down.
- A fixed 1 s delay: requests piled onto the merchant the moment it came back.

doc: docs/decisions/0002-queue-choice.md
section: 0002. Use Redis Streams for the event queue
# 0002. Use Redis Streams for the event queue

- Status: accepted (2025-01-20)

doc: docs/decisions/0002-queue-choice.md
section: 0002. Use Redis Streams for the event queue > Decision
## Decision

The event queue is Redis Streams. A consumer group splits the work across servers, and messages that weren't processed are picked up again via `XPENDING`.

doc: docs/decisions/0002-queue-choice.md
section: 0002. Use Redis Streams for the event queue > Why not SQS
## Why not SQS

- We handle around 100k events a day, which one Redis instance covers easily.
- We already run Redis for sessions, so there's nothing new to operate.
- Keeping events in order per merchant was simpler.

Revisit this if we go past 1M events a day or need multiple regions.

doc: docs/deploy.md
section: Deploying and rolling back
# Deploying and rolling back

doc: docs/deploy.md
section: Deploying and rolling back > Deploying
## Deploying

1. Merging to `main` makes CI build an image and deploy it to staging automatically.
2. Check that `npm run test:e2e -- --env staging` passes against staging.
3. Production deploys are done by a person: `npm run deploy:prod`. The deploy script (`scripts/deploy.sh`) swaps in the new version one server at a time and moves on once that server's `/healthz` returns 200.
4. Whoever deployed posts the version and a short summary of changes in #paymint-deploy.

No production deploys after 4 pm on Fridays.

doc: docs/deploy.md
section: Deploying and rolling back > Rolling back
## Rolling back

If something goes wrong, go straight back to the previous version:

```bash
./scripts/deploy.sh production --rollback
```

`--rollback` redeploys the last image tag that deployed successfully. That alone isn't enough for a deploy that included a DB migration: run the migration's `down` first. PRs with a migration get `[migration]` in the title so they're easy to spot.

doc: docs/incident-response.md
section: Incident response
# Incident response

doc: docs/incident-response.md
section: Incident response > Webhooks keep failing
## Webhooks keep failing

1. Open "Failure rate by merchant" on the dashboard and check whether it's just one merchant.
2. If only one merchant is failing, it's usually their server. Events that fail all 3 retries go to the `dead_letters` table. Once the merchant is back up, replay them with `POST /admin/dead-letters/replay?merchant=<id>`.
3. If every merchant is failing, the problem is on our side. Check the Redis connection and the latest deploy first. If the latest deploy looks suspicious, [roll back](deploy.md#rolling-back).

doc: docs/incident-response.md
section: Incident response > Alerts
## Alerts

When the failure rate stays above 5% for 5 minutes, an alert goes to #paymint-alerts and the on-call engineer gets paged. The on-call rotation is on the team calendar.
